title: Add stable realistic live flashlight mode
objective: Implement a live teleop lighting path for examples/flashlight/run.py that produces stable, realistic dim environment lighting plus physically plausible flashlight behavior: fixed exposure including local-exposure suppression, startup warmup before user control, Lumen GI/reflections retained, inverse-square spotlight support where available, and explicit direct/contact shadow controls.
instructions: Start by directly inspecting the current examples/flashlight/run.py, flashlight_profiles.py/json, run_orbit_collection.py for shared helpers, tests/test_orbit_collection_validation.py, and cpp/unreal_projects/SpearSim/Config/DefaultEngine.ini. Scout could not read these due to policy, so verify all assumptions in code before editing.
Focus implementation on live examples/flashlight/run.py and shared flashlight profile/helpers. Do not redesign orbit collection unless needed for shared profile/test consistency.

Extend fixed exposure for live realistic mode to also suppress local exposure: include r.DefaultFeature.LocalExposure.HighlightContrastScale=0 and r.DefaultFeature.LocalExposure.ShadowContrastScale=0 in launch/runtime config when auto exposure is disabled or realistic live mode is active.

Add startup warmup/gating for live teleop: after map load, scene-light scaling, and flashlight setup, wait out the skylight/Lumen/reflection startup period before entering the user control loop. Make the duration configurable, default around 3 seconds for realistic live mode, and log when live control begins.
Keep Lumen GI/reflections and material response enabled for realistic live mode. Do not reuse validation render settings that disable GI/reflections/SSR/material response.

Add inverse-square spotlight support with robust reflected setters if Unreal exposes UseInverseSquaredFalloff/use_inverse_squared_falloff or equivalent. Preserve safe fallbacks and avoid unsafe property probing that can trigger SPEAR resolveProperty assertions.
Ensure direct flashlight shadow controls remain explicit and safe: cast shadows, dynamic shadows, contact shadow length when supported, and keep --disable-flashlight-contact-shadows as a fallback.
Add or update a profile such as realistic_live_flashlight if it fits the existing profile model. Prefer normal cafeteria v2 as the realistic target; keep dark validation map as diagnostic only.
Add diagnostics/logging for exposure/local exposure config, scene-light scale results, flashlight profile, inverse-square status, shadow/contact-shadow status, and warmup duration.
Add focused unit tests for config construction, profile resolution/overrides, inverse-square setter fallback behavior, and startup warmup sequencing. Run the targeted unittest suite.
constraints: Do not run long Unreal processes; runtime validation will go to Experimenter or the user after Builder.
Do not perform Git operations or commits.
Avoid broad refactors outside the flashlight live/profile path.

artifacts: Live flashlight brightening in cafeteria v2 is most likely a startup temporal-state issue: local exposure remains active, SPEAR forces skylight updates for about 1 second after map load, and Lumen/reflection histories converge while live teleop is already visible. Realistic mode should disable local exposure, warm up before user control, and keep Lumen GI/reflections enabled.

expected_outputs: Builder ResultPacket with changed files, tests run, and the exact live command to validate the realistic stable-lighting mode.
definition_of_done: Live flashlight entry point has a stable realistic startup path with local exposure suppressed, warmup before teleop, Lumen/reflections retained, inverse-square attempt/fallback, direct shadows configured, and focused tests passing.
